extracted.intended_audience: merchants, money-changers and traders (historical/early-modern mercantile practitioners)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and standards for valuing, accounting, and conducting barter and currency-exchange transactions (e.g., wool vs cloth, metal, leather), including how to compute gains/losses, adjust for time (term), convert to cash equivalents, and distinguish lawful vs illicit exchange practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Baratto equale (equality in barter)
rubrics_metrics.description: A barter should be made so that the things exchanged are equal in value (baratto equale); when they are not exactly equal, the parties must compute which part of capital one loses and the other gains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute the portions of each party's capital that are lost and the portions gained by the other; equate gains and losses by reducing to a common denominator and summing the appropriate parts (examples throughout with lana/panno). If one gains X% and the other loses Y%, combine those fractions to determine what must be given to equalize the exchange.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compute gains and losses as parts of capital
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat gains and losses produced by an exchange as fractions (parts) of each party's capital.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Express gains/losses as parts of 100 (percent) or other convenient denominators; when aggregating, add the relevant parts (e.g., 'tal parte del fuo capitale quale io guadagno' and 'tal parte del tuo capitale che tu perdi') and use these to compute what must be transferred so the exchange is fair. Many numerical examples (percenti, decimi, centesimi) demonstrate this.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use common denominators when aggregating fractional parts
rubrics_metrics.description: When comparing or joining fractional gains/losses from different capitals, reduce them to a common denominator before summing or comparing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text repeatedly forms denominators (100, denominato) and instructs joining 'i doi rotti' (two fractions) by bringing them to the same denominator and adding numerators; guidance and examples show how to choose denominators so the parts are comparable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjust valuations for time (termine / mesi)
rubrics_metrics.description: When barter or sale is at term (a termine) rather than cash (a contanti), adjust valuations to account for the time between exchange and payment (months 'mefi'), since goods or money gain/lose value over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute how much each item would gain (or how much capital would multiply) over the period (monthly accumulation examples), compare gains over corresponding months, and convert term prices to present equivalents. Multiple worked examples with months (mefi) show how to multiply gains across months and how to determine equalization over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish and convert a contanti (cash) vs a termine (term) transactions
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat cash sales (a contanti) differently from term sales (a termine); barter involving one cash-priced good and one priced at term must be equalized by converting the term price to its cash equivalent (or vice versa).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask 'quanto tempo Donerà fare quello de la lana a quello dal panno' to determine how many months elapse and compute the monetary effect; examples show converting term valuations into present-value equivalents by using the monthly gain rates and then applying the baratto-equal calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convert goods to cash equivalents using current market values
rubrics_metrics.description: To determine equality, convert each good to its cash value based on current market prices (e.g., lana, panno, canna) and use those cash equivalents in computations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The treatise repeatedly instructs valuing 'la lana a contanti' and 'la canna del panno a contanti' and then forming the baratto-account; account for local market prices, and if a good is sold at cash elsewhere, use that as the basis for comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for processing/finishing effects on value
rubrics_metrics.description: Processing or finishing (e.g., curarne/leather finishing, fulling, dressing) changes the value of a commodity and must be taken into account when valuing for barter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples (curarne vs ferro, pelle a contanti, 'termene mdt.4...') show that the same raw material and processed product have different valuations; when one item is finished or processed and the other not, adjust the valuation to reflect the added (or subtracted) worth from finishing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classify types of exchange and apply appropriate rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Different kinds of exchange (several 'modi' of cambio/exchange are identified) require different treatments—distinguish among real/fictitious, minute/common, daily/from-a-territory, and so on, and apply the specified norms for each.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text enumerates 'le specie di cambi eifer quattro' and other distinctions; practitioners must identify which mode applies (e.g., cambio da giornata, cambio comune) because each has its customary valuation and legality rules. Use the sectioned rules to decide which computation and practices are proper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use bankers, bills of exchange, and letters with clear terms
rubrics_metrics.description: When using a bill of exchange ('Ira de cambio', lettera di cambio), specify place, payer, tenor, time, and any replicatory claims; the instrument must contain enough detail (name, place, time, tenor) to be honored and to indicate payment instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The treatise instructs naming the place to which the bill is directed, the tenor, and whether it is payable at first, second, etc. If one replicates payments, preserve documentary evidence ('la lettera e copia') and follow the customary forms to avoid disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for locality, abundance, and scarcity in exchange rates
rubrics_metrics.description: Exchange/currency values and commodity prices differ by location and by abundance/scarcity; adjust valuations accordingly when converting or transporting goods between markets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text explains that local demand/supply ('abundanzia e carctia') changes rates and that merchants should buy where abundant and sell where scarce; exchange rates between places (and thus values in local currency) must be considered when computing fair barter or conversion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid illicit, abusive, or reproachable exchange practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain mercantile practices are illicit or reprehensible; merchants must avoid fraud, abusive manipulations of exchange, and other condemned behaviours in forming exchange deals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author warns against 'illiciti e rep2oban'' and abusive tricks in exchange; follow the lawful mercantile customs and proper forms so that transactions are legitimate and defensible (moral/legal admonitions and examples appear in the text).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat repeated barters and cumulative gains multiplicatively
rubrics_metrics.description: If goods are repeatedly bartered or held across many periods, gains accumulate multiplicatively and must be calculated as such rather than simply added.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Worked examples show that monthly gains multiply over time ('se multiplica... parti in... e virate'), and one must compute the compound effect across months/mefi to find what the goods will be worth at the later date before comparing or equalizing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Round and select practical denominators for computations
rubrics_metrics.description: When performing the arithmetic of parts and fractions, choose convenient denominators (100, denominato, centesimi) and round appropriately to produce workable equalizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manual uses denominators like 100 and instructs forming denominators on the binomial and extracting residues; practical computational choices (centi, decimi) are recommended in examples to ease calculation and to determine the part to transfer for equalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure equivalence in quality and kind when substituting goods
rubrics_metrics.description: When substituting one good for another (e.g., one piece of cloth for wool), ensure they are equivalent in quality, measure (canna, peso), and other relevant attributes; if not, adjust valuation accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples about 'la canna del panno' versus 'lana' stress comparing the same kinds and qualities; if qualities differ, compute the proper adjustment (price differentials, months-to-multiplication) rather than assuming nominal equality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record terms and keep documentary proof of agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Use written letters, copies, and clear notation of terms so that the obligations and the valuation method are evidenced ('la lettera e copia', 'fatta la coptia'), enabling enforcement and later clarification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text emphasizes writing (letters, copies) describing the exchange, its terms, and payment instructions; documentary clarity prevents disputes and supports claims in case of non-payment or disagreement.
